examples: The city council voted to ban smoking in all public parks.
شورای شهر رأی داد که سیگار کشیدن را در تمام پارک‌های عمومی ممنوع کند.
Many schools ban the use of mobile phones during exams.
بسیاری از مدارس استفاده از تلفن همراه را در طول امتحانات ممنوع می‌کنند.
The government decided to ban the import of certain plastic products.
دولت تصمیم گرفت واردات برخی محصولات پلاستیکی را ممنوع کند.
miniContext: Governments and institutions sometimes ban things that are considered harmful to public health or safety. For example, several countries ban smoking in restaurants and other enclosed spaces. When officials ban a product or activity, they usually explain the reasons behind the decision so that people understand and follow the new rule.

examples: Each salesperson must meet a monthly quota of fifty new customers.
هر فروشنده باید سهمیه ماهانه پنجاه مشتری جدید را تکمیل کند.
The factory increased its production quota for the holiday season.
کارخانه سهمیه تولید خود را برای فصل تعطیلات افزایش داد.
The country set a strict quota on the number of refugees it would accept.
آن کشور سهمیه سختگیرانه‌ای برای تعداد پناهندگانی که می‌پذیرفت تعیین کرد.
miniContext: A quota is a fixed limit or target that a person or organization must reach or stay within. Companies often set a sales quota for their employees to encourage steady performance. Governments may also use a quota to control immigration numbers or the amount of goods that can be imported each year.

examples: Fresh water is not abundant in this desert region.
آب شیرین در این منطقه کویری فراوان نیست.
The garden produced an abundant harvest of tomatoes this summer.
باغ امسال تابستان محصول فراوانی از گوجه‌فرنگی داد.
Wildlife is abundant in the national park, especially near the river.
حیات وحش در پارک ملی فراوان است، به‌خصوص نزدیک رودخانه.
miniContext: When resources are abundant, there is more than enough to go around. Rainforests, for instance, are known for abundant plant and animal life because of their warm, wet climate. People often take abundant resources for granted until they become scarce.

examples: A sponge can absorb a surprising amount of water.
یک اسفنج می‌تواند مقدار شگفت‌انگیزی آب جذب کند.
Students need time to absorb new information before the next lesson.
دانش‌آموزان برای جذب اطلاعات جدید قبل از درس بعدی به زمان نیاز دارند.
The thick walls of the old building absorb sound very well.
دیوارهای ضخیم آن ساختمان قدیمی صدا را خیلی خوب جذب می‌کنند.
miniContext: To absorb something means to take it in gradually, whether it is a liquid, a sound, or an idea. Plants absorb water and nutrients through their roots, while a curious mind can absorb new knowledge from books and conversations. Material that can absorb shock is often used in sports shoes and car bumpers.

examples: Formal clothing is appropriate for a job interview.
لباس رسمی برای مصاحبه شغلی مناسب است.
The city council voted to appropriate funds for a new public library.
شورای شهر رأی داد تا بودجه‌ای برای کتابخانه عمومی جدید اختصاص دهد.
Her comment was not appropriate given the serious mood of the meeting.
با توجه به فضای جدی جلسه، نظر او مناسب نبود.
miniContext: Appropriate usually describes something suitable for a particular situation, but it can also be a verb meaning to set money or resources aside for a specific purpose. Choosing appropriate words for a formal letter is different from the casual language used with friends. A city government might appropriate funds for a project only after careful debate about priorities.

examples: Experts estimate that the renovation will cost about ten thousand dollars.
کارشناسان برآورد می‌کنند که بازسازی حدود ده هزار دلار هزینه خواهد داشت.
Please estimate how long the trip will take before we leave.
لطفاً قبل از حرکت، برآورد کنید سفر چقدر طول می‌کشد.
We should estimate the total cost before signing the contract.
باید قبل از امضای قرارداد، هزینه کل را برآورد کنیم.
miniContext: When exact numbers are not available, people often estimate based on experience and available data. Before buying a house, for instance, a buyer might ask an inspector to estimate the cost of necessary repairs. Although an estimate is never completely precise, a careful one still helps with planning and budgeting.

examples: She felt uneasy walking home alone after dark.
او هنگام پیاده‌روی تنها در شب احساس نگرانی می‌کرد.
There was an uneasy silence in the room after the announcement.
بعد از آن اعلامیه، سکوتی ناآرام در اتاق حاکم شد.
He grew uneasy when his boss asked to speak with him privately.
وقتی رئیسش از او خواست خصوصی صحبت کنند، نگران شد.
miniContext: Feeling uneasy usually means sensing that something is slightly wrong, even without clear proof. A sudden change in someone's tone of voice, for example, can make a listener uneasy. Writers often use an uneasy atmosphere to build tension before something unexpected happens in the story.

examples: The sudden fire alarm caused panic among the students.
زنگ آتش‌نشانی ناگهانی باعث وحشت میان دانش‌آموزان شد.
Don't panic; we still have time to catch the train.
وحشت نکن؛ هنوز وقت داریم تا به قطار برسیم.
In a panic, she forgot where she had left her keys.
او از شدت دستپاچگی یادش رفت کلیدهایش را کجا گذاشته است.
miniContext: Panic is a sudden, overwhelming feeling of fear that can make it hard to think clearly. When the lights went out during the concert, panic spread quickly through the crowd. Emergency workers are trained to stay calm so that their own panic does not make a dangerous situation worse.

examples: Farmers harvest wheat in late summer when the grain is dry.
کشاورزان گندم را در اواخر تابستان، وقتی دانه خشک است، برداشت می‌کنند.
This year's harvest was smaller than usual because of the drought.
محصول امسال به دلیل خشکسالی کمتر از حد معمول بود.
Workers need to harvest the grapes before the first frost arrives.
کارگران باید انگورها را قبل از رسیدن اولین یخبندان برداشت کنند.
miniContext: Harvest refers to both the act of gathering ripe crops and the crops themselves once they are gathered. In many farming communities, the whole family helps harvest the fields during a few busy weeks each year. A good harvest depends on the right combination of sunlight, rain, and soil quality.

examples: Please calculate the total cost of the trip, including fuel and food.
لطفاً هزینه کل سفر، شامل سوخت و غذا را محاسبه کن.
Engineers calculate the exact weight a bridge can safely support.
مهندسان وزن دقیقی را که یک پل می‌تواند با امنیت تحمل کند محاسبه می‌کنند.
We need to calculate how many chairs will fit in the hall.
باید محاسبه کنیم چند صندلی در سالن جا می‌شود.
miniContext: To calculate something means to work out a number or an answer using math or careful reasoning. Before renting a new apartment, it is wise to calculate the total monthly cost, including rent, utilities, and transportation. Accountants calculate taxes and expenses every year to make sure a company's finances are accurate.

examples: The dog waited patiently for a morsel of food to fall from the table.
سگ با صبر منتظر بود تا لقمه‌ای از غذا از روی میز بیفتد.
She savored every morsel of the rich chocolate cake.
او از هر لقمه آن کیک شکلاتی غنی لذت می‌برد.
After the long hike, even a small morsel of bread tasted delicious.
بعد از آن پیاده‌روی طولانی، حتی یک تکه کوچک نان هم خیلی خوشمزه بود.
miniContext: A morsel is a small piece or bite of something, usually food. During a famine, people may fight over a single morsel of bread. In everyday use, the word can also describe a tiny bit of information, as in a morsel of gossip.

examples: The company received a threat from a former employee after the layoffs.
شرکت بعد از تعدیل نیرو، یک تهدید از یک کارمند سابق دریافت کرد.
Climate change poses a serious threat to coastal cities around the world.
تغییرات آب‌وهوایی تهدیدی جدی برای شهرهای ساحلی در سراسر جهان است.
The coach warned the players that losing focus could be a threat to their chances of winning.
مربی به بازیکنان هشدار داد که از دست دادن تمرکز می‌تواند تهدیدی برای شانس برد آن‌ها باشد.
miniContext: A threat is something that could cause harm or danger in the future. Businesses must constantly watch for a threat to their reputation, whether from competitors or negative reviews. Police take any threat of violence seriously, even when it seems unlikely to be carried out.
